rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent low-rise bar with one dominant mass and a readable notch/cut, so it clears basic massing legibility. However, the public void is weakly articulated, and the access-edge response is not yet forceful enough for the neighborhood-living brief: the notch is present but does not yet produce a clearly occupied, publicly legible ground threshold aligned with the verified frontage. In four views the object remains mostly a compact extruded volume with a localized incision, rather than a robust active-edge composition with a stronger court/terrace/undercut hierarchy. It also does not strongly express section-based program logic beyond generic massing, so program_fit_hard_pass fails even though the silhouette is not incoherent. The most transferable precedent move is to deepen the access-side carve or terrace so the ground edge becomes usable public space while preserving the dominant bar.
